Random walk penalties for smooth terms

Source: R/rw_penalty.R
rw_penalty.Rd

Creates a first or second order random walk penalty matrix for the levels of an ordered covariate, for use with the Markov random field (mrf) basis of mgcv. This is the recommended way to include smooth terms in efp: the basis and the penalty are both sparse, so models are quick to fit even when there are many levels.

Usage

rw_penalty(levels, order = 1)

Arguments

levels

the levels of the covariate, in order, and assumed to be equally spaced. A level is needed for every step of the random walk, including any for which there are no data.

order

the order of the random walk, 1 or 2

Value

a square matrix with one row and column for each level, with the levels as dimnames. The matrix has an attribute, null.space, which is a basis for the functions which are not penalised.

Details

A first order random walk (order = 1) penalises the differences between neighbouring levels, and shrinks towards a constant. A second order random walk (order = 2) penalises the second differences, and shrinks towards a linear trend. In both cases the standard deviation estimated by efp is the standard deviation of the steps of the random walk, on the logit scale.

To use the penalty, the covariate must be a factor with the same levels as the penalty, see the examples.

Examples

rw_penalty(1:5)
#>    1  2  3  4  5
#> 1  1 -1  0  0  0
#> 2 -1  2 -1  0  0
#> 3  0 -1  2 -1  0
#> 4  0  0 -1  2 -1
#> 5  0  0  0 -1  1
#> attr(,"null.space")
#>            [,1]
#> [1,] -0.4472136
#> [2,] -0.4472136
#> [3,] -0.4472136
#> [4,] -0.4472136
#> [5,] -0.4472136
rw_penalty(1:5, order = 2)
#>    1  2  3  4  5
#> 1  1 -2  1  0  0
#> 2 -2  5 -4  1  0
#> 3  1 -4  6 -4  1
#> 4  0  1 -4  5 -2
#> 5  0  0  1 -2  1
#> attr(,"null.space")
#>            [,1]          [,2]
#> [1,] -0.4472136 -6.324555e-01
#> [2,] -0.4472136 -3.162278e-01
#> [3,] -0.4472136 -7.177699e-18
#> [4,] -0.4472136  3.162278e-01
#> [5,] -0.4472136  6.324555e-01

# a first order random walk over day of the year
data(ef_data)
ef_data$sampleID <- factor(paste(ef_data$date, ef_data$siteID,
                                 ef_data$lifestage, ef_data$species))
days <- min(ef_data$doy):max(ef_data$doy)
ef_data$fdoy <- factor(ef_data$doy, levels = days)
rw1 <- rw_penalty(days)

m1 <- efp(count ~ lifestage + s(fdoy, bs = "mrf", xt = list(penalty = rw1)),
          data = ef_data, pass = pass, id = sampleID)
m1
#> 
#> Call:
#> efp(formula = count ~ lifestage + s(fdoy, bs = "mrf", xt = list(penalty = rw1)), 
#>     data = ef_data, pass = pass, id = sampleID)
#> 
#> Formula:
#> count ~ lifestage + s(fdoy, bs = "mrf", xt = list(penalty = rw1))
#> <environment: 0x55e79ed74488>
#> 
#> Random effects:
#>               Estimate Std. Error
#> sigma s(fdoy) 0.001289    0.01585
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#>               Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z^2|)
#> (Intercept)     0.6820    0.07131   9.564  1.138e-21
#> lifestageParr   0.6212    0.10292   6.036  1.577e-09
#>
